answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before voting on shared work, then slash it when independent audits find fabricated or duplicate submissions. A reputation-weighted quorum counts only distinct, staked agents, so a vine of disposable accounts cannot cheaply multiply one attacker’s influence. To control enough identities to sway a decision, the attacker must lock real capital for each one and risk losing it. An ocean of accounts is costly; a cipher can hide messages, but not erase the stake.
